content:
I wonder why all files containing generalities about Filters, like
## Mathlib.Order.Filter.Basic
are in the Order folder. I guess @Yaël Dillies has an idea :smirk: , but I'm not sure to grasp to what extent they should be there.
Historical. Probably Order.Filter should contain the theory of docs#PFilter instead
And (beyond the horrible pain of refactoring it, which I'm not sure I'd like to experience), would you have any objection to moving them to, say, Data?
Data? I would have put them in Topology since filters do not contain data in a meaningful way. Sets neither, for the record
Well, I was suggesting Databecause this is where Setsare. I agree that this is perhaps strange, but at least it seems to me that we agree that Filters and Sets should be in the same place.
For Topology, I'm a bit sceptical since their use in topology is of course crucial but they make full sense independently of it...
What about MeasureTheory.ae? This filter is completely unrelated to topology :melting_face:
Top-level folder Filter/?

The maths of sets: SetTheory
The maths of measures: MeasureTheory
The maths of filters: Topology FilterTheory
Personally I'd consider most of the things in SetTheory to be about order theory instead
Whatever we do, please do not add anything into Data.
Why not? Set is in Data and Filter feels very similar to Set.
Indeed filters are not limited to topology, they should be somewhere close to Set.
But Set has nothing to do in Data, it’s a historical accident.
What about a top folder Set containing both sets and Filter? I would feel ok in having filters within sets, because they're generalised sets.
It'd be a bit weird to have both Set and SetTheory, no?
I agree that the mathematics of docs#Set and the mathematics which mathematicians generally call "set theory" are two very different things. But it would still feel weird to me.

I would find it ok, honestly. As a mathematician with no training in set theory, I've always felt ok in speaking about sets although I would declare myself completely ignorant in the discipline of Set Theory. It's like having "number systems" containing facts about Nat, Int, Rat, ZMOD and then a Number Theory folder.
How about we rename Set to Subset :-)

Kevin Buzzard said:

How about we rename Set to Subset :-)

when I talk about Set Nat informally it's always "a set of naturals" and not "a subset of the set of all naturals"

Patrick Massot said:

But Set has nothing to do in Data, it’s a historical accident.

There are a few things in Data that seem like they shouldn't (FunLike, SetLike, some of the Fin* folders). Maybe we need a top level folder that contains all of these + Set and Filter?
Slightly tongue in cheek: Basic/
